author: WP19
summary: Explains how CnaTests, standalone renderer programs, isolation helpers, negative compilation and script gates compose, and the discovery/selection/execution/verdict model. The testing architecture pages already had the assembly, discovery and skip mechanics; the self-asserting filters, three gating layers, build-versus-registration and label statistics, tool-versus-test helpers, the WILL_FAIL mechanism and the stage model are new on the test-populations deep dive. The single-binary claim and the build-far-more-than-register claim were corrected.

sections.heading: Standalone examples are a separate corpus
Why some tests need another process
Compilation failure can be the oracle

concepts.text: CNA's test system is a composition of one aggregate GoogleTest binary, hundreds of standalone renderer executables, process-isolation harnesses, negative compilation and script-based structural gates; interpreting a result starts with knowing which layer produced it.
tokens: Five kinds of executable evidence coexist

concepts.text: cmake/UnitTests.cmake recursively globs module tests, renderer-family tests, shared renderer-helper tests and top-level tests into CnaTests; the claim that no per-module GoogleTest executable exists is corrected: 22 focused EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL binaries are built from the same object groups but are not CTest registrations.

A long explicit filter chain narrows the glob: standalone C API and module-probe programs, optional Inspector and media cases, implementation-specific platform and audio suites, POSIX-helper tests on hosts without them, Net and GamerServices when disabled, build-time tool tests and renderer-local suites of absent families.

Several filters assert themselves, which makes filtering part of the build contract: with CNA_ENABLE_NET=OFF the surviving list is walked and a leftover network or GamerServices source is a configure FATAL_ERROR, and a group without a focused-target name or with a missing dependency target also stops the configure.

target.evidence: cmake/UnitTests.cmake (_cna_disabled_net_test loop; No focused test target name; requires missing target)

concepts.text: GoogleTest cases reach CTest through gtest_discover_tests(... DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST): discovery runs the built binary at test time, so the complete CTest list does not exist at configure time.

The discovered cases run with the repository root as working directory, pinned after cases failed to find tests/assets when CTest launched them from the runtime-output directory; a source count and a ctest -N count therefore answer different questions.
tokens: pins the repository root as the working directory

concepts.text: A configure enters one renderer family or a compatible CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERERS set; renderer-local source filtering tests membership in CNA_RENDERER_IDENTITIES, so a multi-renderer CnaTests keeps the suites of every compiled family, not only the default.
tokens: Membership in the compiled set, not the default identity, decides

concepts.text: Some families contribute portable policy suites even when their native implementation is host-gated; suites guard their bodies on CNA_RENDERER_<X> or CNA_RENDERER_PRESENT_<X> so they compile whenever the family is in the build.
No supported configuration implies "all renderers"; a result that omits the compiled set and the active runtime identity cannot be interpreted.
tokens: is not a statement any single run can support

concepts.text: Renderer gating has three layers: source filtering decides which families' GoogleTests enter CnaTests, CMake conditions decide which standalone executables and CTests are registered, and runtime pre-flight may return the skip code 77 when no display is usable.

Exit 77 is reported as skipped rather than failed so headless machines do not turn a missing display into a renderer defect; a green summary may therefore contain no executed pixel comparison, and reports must keep skip counts and the display setup.
tokens: A skipped test is not feature evidence

concepts.section: Standalone examples are a separate corpus
concepts.text: Files named *_test.cpp under renderer examples are not GoogleTest sources: family macros build each as its own executable with main() and optionally register it; many consume shared fixtures from modules/graphics/examples so one renderer can expose a defect while others act as controls.

concepts.section: Standalone examples are a separate corpus
concepts.text: Building and registering are independent statements; the claim that some renderers build far more executables than they register is corrected: lexical build-helper and registration calls are near one-to-one in every family at TARGET (EasyGL 357/356, Vulkan 384/385, SDL_GPU 122/135).
tokens: Building and registering are two statements

concepts.section: Standalone examples are a separate corpus
concepts.text: Labels are uneven: GraphicsSmoke is attached across families, while Vulkan, EasyGL and SDL_RENDERER label almost none of their hundreds of registrations, so ctest -L EasyGL does not select the EasyGL corpus and name selectors are the reliable ones.

concepts.section: Why some tests need another process
concepts.text: Failures involving process-global state (SDL shutdown, the mixer's global owner, GamerServices dispatch, network peers) are tested by spawning small helper executables whose absolute paths are baked into the test objects, giving a clean address space.
tokens: Their paths are baked into the object group as compile definitions

concepts.section: Why some tests need another process
concepts.text: Other executables beside the harnesses are tools, not tests (XNB audio metadata dumper, XWB inspector, FNA-reference dump, devices microbenchmark, the fuzz harnesses); their presence does not put them into a test run, so the question is who invokes a target under which configuration.

concepts.section: Compilation failure can be the oracle
concepts.text: cna_strict_xna_api_leak_check is EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL; the CTest StrictXnaApiSurfaceLeakCheck_MustFailToCompile runs a build of it with WILL_FAIL TRUE, so the test passes only when the compiler rejects the deliberate CNAEXT use and successful compilation is the regression.

concepts.section: Compilation failure can be the oracle
concepts.text: Fifteen module probes apply the idea to linking: each builds a minimal consumer of one alias and a closure test inspects the generated link line against forbidden libraries; the probe shows the target works, the closure shows it works for the right architectural reason.
tokens: inspects the probe's generated link line for forbidden and required inputs

concepts.text: A reliable report separates four stages: discovery (which sources and runtime-expanded cases existed), selection (which filter, label, renderer and feature options chose them), execution (whether the intended executable, display, GPU, browser or translation layer engaged) and verdict (which oracle declared pass, fail or skip).

target.evidence: framing; CNA-specific checks per stage listed on the page

concepts.text: The stage model explains apparent contradictions: a source can exist but be filtered out, a target build but not be registered, a CTest register but skip, and a program pass while running through the wrong graphics translation layer.
tokens: a program can pass while running through the wrong graphics translation layer
